utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASESSE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. Yes, Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. With your leave, before we begin the examination of the witness, I should like to raise one question relating to the procedure; that is, the testimony by the accused, if I may. Vlatko Kupreskic's Defence has announced the testimony given by the accused at the end of the examination. Meanwhile, the Prosecutor's office has also announced the production of additional evidence relative to the defence presented here on behalf of Vlatko Kupreskic. It is the interest of the Defence that when the accused presents, that all evidence brought against him be produced, and my question is does the Trial Chamber allow the accused to testify after the Prosecution has produced all the evidence, or does the accused need to give his evidence before that? So that is my question. I might also mention that in the legal system of the accused, this is resolved in the manner that the accused is given the floor last, and he is entitled to testify with regard to all the evidence adduced against him. So this is my question. I would appreciate very much your instructions in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASESSE
utterances.text: I'll ask Mr. Terrier what he thinks about this matter, and then we will make a ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that the Rules of Procedure are quite clear on how the hearing goes. First the Prosecutor's evidence, and then the Defence evidence needs to be presented before anything else, and I believe that Mr. Par asking the accused to testify as the last one in this case, whereas the Prosecution still has to submit some of their refutals seems to me contrary to the Rules of Procedure, and I do not think that it should be accepted here at the International Tribunal. The Defence has the last word in all the judicial systems that I know, but not of the accused himself, and therefore the Defence here should, through the Defence counsel, have the last word, and they have this right. I believe that the rights of the accused in this manner are fully respected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASESSE
utterances.text: Let me say that on the last point, I think actually even in Nuremberg, the accused had the last word, but to make a statement, not to give evidence. So we have to make a distinction between giving evidence and making a final statement. I think this is what happened in Nuremberg, to the best of my recollection. So the accused gave evidence, and then before the Court decided to make a ruling, to issue a verdict, they were allowed to have a final word. Therefore, this distinction, I think, is important. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Our ruling is as follows: According to the Rules of Procedure, of course the accused, if they are called by Defence counsel as witnesses in their own behalf, of course they have to give evidence at the end of the Defence case, so before the Prosecutor starts with the rebuttal, with rebuttal witnesses. So therefore they cannot give evidence at the very end. However, this does not exclude that the Defence counsel can call the accused as witnesses in rejoinder after the rebuttal. They can be called again to testify in court, and on top of that, they can also make, if they wish to do so, a final statement, which is, as I say, just a statement on their own position. I hope this position is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now -- yes, Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday, as I was examining Finka Bralo, I always mentioned the time, and the witness herself spoke of twenty to six, that is 5.40. However, I hear from my colleagues that what the transcript says, it is twenty to five, or 4.40. I believe that either the transcript is wrong or perhaps it was my slip of the tongue, and will you please bear this in mind, because we have spoken of 5.40, of twenty to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It was your slip of the tongue at the end of the evidence which created that confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will make the record straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. Mr. President, one more thing: Will the registry please tell me, Exhibit D35/4, has this been admitted into evidence, and is it properly filed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, actually I was about to raise this matter. I think you forgot yesterday, because you were tired, and we were all a bit tired, to propose that it should be admitted into evidence, but I was about to ask the Prosecution whether they had any objection. I hope not. No. So it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is not 35/4 but -- it's not 35/4 but 34/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. This one, Counsel Susak, this one? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is the aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. We can now start with our last witness, Mr. Bralo. Good morning. Could you please stand and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Susak:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bralo.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Court your full name, where you were born, and where do you live?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Bralo, the village of Santici, Vitez. I was born on the 20th of February, 1950.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom do you live with in Santici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I live with my wife, Finka Bralo, and my two sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, what did you do in 1993, sometime in the beginning of that year? That is, what was your occupation, or where did you work?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I'm a worker, and I worked for the British UNPROFOR as a stoker at the beginning of the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told us you worked at the UNPROFOR and employed by the British Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife, was she employed by the British UNPROFOR at the same time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, she also worked for the UNPROFOR in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when had you been working for UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It was from the beginning of the season, so it must have been October, I believe, and I was to work for them until the end of the season; that is, until the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you give us the dates, please?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: From the 1st of October --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, not'93; '92, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So between the 1st of October, 1992, if I understand you properly, until?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Until the 15th of April. That is, '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now can we ask the usher, please, to show a document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D35/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo, can you see this document? What does it say?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, of course I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it mean? You also have the English translation, and you also have it in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: This is a document certifying that I worked for the British Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is that you were employed there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, that I was employed there, as I have said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you read the last sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: This one here, you mean? "It is certified hereby that Anto Bralo is employed at Vitez camp as the boiler stoker and that he is thereby authorised to enter the camp." This is what I was given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Will you tell us, while you were employed by the UNPROFOR, did you work both in daytime and at night?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I covered the first and the third shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So both during daytime and at night time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will the usher please show now the second document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D36/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo, will you tell us, what does this document mean?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: This document means that I worked -- they translate it into Croatian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, but read it to us in Croatian. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It is with regard that "I have to give you notice of the termination of your service from the 25th of April 1993."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a certification by UNPROFOR that it was the termination of your service?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, that my service was to be terminated on the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the Prosecutor does not trust these translations, I also have the originals, if need be, to confirm the authenticity, if that proves necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see it is not, so, Mr. Bralo, I shall continue with my examination. Will you tell us, where were you at the time of the first conflict, that is, on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: On the 20th -- on the 19th of October we went to the wood to fell some trees, to cut wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the wood. And where is that wood?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It is Kruscica, and I, Anto Bralo, Franjo Kovac, Mirsad Osmancevic, and my late brother, Ivo Bralo, went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take part in the first conflict? You said that you went to cut wood.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I did not take part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any houses were damaged in that first conflict?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: In that first conflict, I learnt it when I arrived next morning, Drago Josipovic's stable was on fire, whether his wife's or his mother's, but at any rate, it was on fire. And on his house there were bullet marks, on the walls of his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you -- that was at the time when you were employed by the UNPROFOR, and while you were in Santici, did you ever go on guard?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I did it, but seldom. I did not have an opportunity, since I was employed, so the people simply relieved me of that, as I simply couldn't do both things; that is, both work and stand guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were employed with UNPROFOR, did you have an UNPROFOR uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was given it by a soldier as a kind of work clothes which I wore when I was down there in the boiler room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wear it all the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, well, I would wear it on my way back home and on my way to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we shall move on to the 16th of April, 1993. Will you tell us, where were you on the day before that, that is, on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, I came home with my wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you come from?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I came from UNPROFOR, from the battalion for which I worked. So we got home, we fed our livestock, had coffee. Of course, in the evening we went to bed and tried to get some rest so as to go to work next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you go to bed?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It was between 10.00 and 11.00. That is when we usually went to bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now will you please tell us about your experience on the 16th of April. How did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, I was woken up by gunfire. I got up, went out to the balcony, upset, very anxious, frightened, not knowing what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone come to your house that morning?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Franjo Kovac and his wife and one child came to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you come -- did they come to your door, or what?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: They came to our entrance. Mrs. Kata Kovac and her child entered the house and Franjo Kovac stayed outside, and we just discussed the situation and what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone on the road above?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic at the crossroad, some 50 or 60 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they moving or standing?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Franjo Kovac and I were talking what to do and how to go about it. We decided to go to Mirsad Osmancevic's stable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you moving in the direction of Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic as they were standing at the crossroad?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, we were. But they started to the right, towards Mirsad Osmancevic's house, where Anto Papic lived, to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they went up, and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: We started towards Anto Papic's house, towards his stable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, you went in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. That is, we went to the left and they went to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you left Anto and Franjo Kovac behind the stable of --

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, Anto Papic's stable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see after that? Did you see anyone come down the road? Did you see Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic after that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: A few minutes later, perhaps some ten minutes later, I saw two or three children crying and coming. I saw Hasim Ahmic and his wife and his daughter-in-law and three children, and Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic were going by the side to Anto Papic's house, and they all entered Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, when did you see Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic again, and did you see them again at all?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them again. I saw them again. They came after a while and we talked for some time. Franjo Kovac, Anto Papic, Drago Josipovic, and I were talking. We were standing by the stable. We were all very worried, and Anto Papic was -- had tears in his eyes. And I was very upset, because we were all neighbours. We knew all those people, and we were on very good terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that morning, you mean that you were all at home, Anto Papic, you, Franjo Kovac, and Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. We were at home, and Drago Josipovic too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are still referring to the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that you were next to the stable, and what were your movements after that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I start to my house, down to -- and then to Nikola Omazic's house, rather, where Franjo Kovac was staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then go home?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, then I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you look from Nikola Omazic's house in the direction of your house, there is a field there. So is there a lane, is there a path to go to your house without crossing the field?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it go down to your house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, there is a certain slope, and you go down it to your house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife told us yesterday that from the terrace from which she observed the situation and the area in front of Nikola Omazic's house, that in order to get a better view of the road, that she moved some five or six metres from the house. So what does it mean, she wanted to get a better view and being on the terrace?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, my wife is rather short, so in order to see better --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please slow down, Mr. Bralo. Your house is dug into the ground?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite correct. It is dug into it. It is on the level with the field which is above it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the terrace?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, the terrace is slightly higher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you move forward towards the lane, is that higher than-- is that ground higher than the terrace?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, it is. She went out into the meadow, some five or six metres into the meadow, and then she could see the road better because it is all clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it is all clear. It is an exposed area. So what kind of ground do we have towards the road and towards Musafer Puscul's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, it is all exposed area, their houses, but they are scattered to the left and right. So if you come out two or three metres of the meadow, then you can see towards the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can see this whole area, and you also say that houses are visible and there is a good view of the areas between the houses?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing on the 16th of April, '93, during that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I moved between my house and Anto's house and to the stable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is where you spent most of your time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, that is where we spent most of our time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Papic, Franjo Kovac, Drago Josipovic, because we were there all together within a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where else did you go? Did you go anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, then Marija Papic called us because she has some livestock, so Anto Papic and I went to feed her livestock. We fed pigs and poultry, hens, and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether, apart from (redacted) and her family, on the 16th of April, were there any other Muslims in Anto Papic's house on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, there was Ramic. I mean Ramic's family was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please recall the names, Ramic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, Hasim -- no, I mean Cazim. Cazim Ramic, I think that was his name, something like that. I know him as Cazim Ramic, I believe he was. Then his wife, his daughter-in-law and two grandchildren were there. Those were my next-door neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: There was also - Hasim also registered that, and his wife and his daughter-in-law and grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you already told us that.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: There (redacted), with her mother and two children. I saw her in Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: There was some other refugees who must have fled from Jajce beforehand and were staying with friends or somebody, and they were also there. There were quite a number of people in the house. I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Bralo, do you know if Mirsad Osmancevic and his family were also in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they were there on the 16th, Mirsad Osmanac and his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Osmanac or what?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Osmancevic, Osmancevic, but we called him Osmanac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he is Osmancevic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. His wife, and he also had three sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us whether he left Anto Papic's house on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he did. His wife, I can't remember her name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't matter?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: His wife and three children crossed Radak's Bridge and went to Jozo Cerkez's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mirsad Osmancevic go in that direction?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Mirsad Osmancevic went, yes. Drago Josipovic went with him because he wanted to be with his wife and children at Jozo Cerkez's house because they had very close relations, they were very good friends, so they went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mirsad Osmancevic have a young child, younger than a year old?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he did, a little son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that child have lived under the conditions prevailing in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No. It was not good for adults either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the reason why his family left for Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, very probably, because the living conditions were much better, much more comfortable. That house is spacious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how Mirsad Osmancevic went to Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic took him as far as Jozo Cerkez's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he help him in any other way?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He gave him a vest, the vest he was wearing. He gave it to him so that he would be safer going to Jozo Cerkez's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long he stayed up there and whether he knew anyone there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, he didn't stay very long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who didn't stay very long?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Mirsad Osmancevic, with his wife and children. They came back soon, after an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they come back?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: They came back to Anto Papic's house, which they had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see it myself, but I heard that a soldier threatened Jozo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jozo Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, Jozo Cerkez, that he would blow his house up if Mirsad Osmancevic was there, so Mirsad Osmancevic came back to Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any problems on his way back?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come back on his own or did his family come with him?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: They came back together, and they came to Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they settle down in that house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and they spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us -- but I have to say that you and Mirsad Osmancevic had gone to cut wood, so I conclude that you cooperated, that you worked together. Could you tell us something about him? Was he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Muslim by nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any other information about him?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I know that before the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims, he used to go to a place called Preocica for the training of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Most probably soldiers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as they called it, because I talked to him but he never wanted to discuss it with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He trained the younger soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he still an officer in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I heard about it, but I didn't discuss it with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I heard that he was some kind of senior officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With a rank?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, with a rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that sometimes you would patrol, but that you didn't have time. Who kept records in that area as to the patrols?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It was Nikica Grebenar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he patrol?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: He had other duties. He was some kind of inspector. He had more to do, so he didn't have to patrol and he couldn't do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, the area where you patrolled?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: From Anto Papic's house to the road; that is, to Jozo Santic's house, Drago Josipovic's house, because his house is next to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where Drago Josipovic's house is next to the road?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since these are hamlets with a special configuration of terrain, could you tell us, along the route you mentioned in the direction where the houses of (redacted), Asim Ahmic, and (redacted) are located toward the River Lasva parallel to the route you took, who patrolled there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Nenad Santic did. They patrolled the other hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was a special route, a special area where other people patrolled?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now talking about the road. Do you know where the houses of (redacted), are located?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us, their house across the road to the north, who patrolled there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Slavko Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was another group of people from that hamlet who patrolled, and who was the leader of the patrol?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Slavko Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slavko Papic then. So above the road is the area where they patrolled, and where (redacted), and Asim Ahmic lived is where a group of people kept guard, and Nenad Santic lived there as well?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, Nenad Santic lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the reserves?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the reserves, but sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were in the reserves?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were in the reserves, could you please tell when you were mobilised for the first time, if you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 19 -- on the 19th of April, 1993, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the second conflict?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was mobilised with you then?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Franjo Kovac, Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you speak a little closer to the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic, Anto Bralo, Franjo Kovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Nikica Grebenar mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Nikica Grebenar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, you really don't have to go on. I would like, Mr. President, to ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit number -- just a moment, please. I think it's 353. Yes, this is the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at page 78? I apologise. Page 84. Have you opened it? Mr. Bralo, on page 84 you can see a name somewhere in the middle, a little down. Would you please find your name? I think it's number 7.562. Have you found your name?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the document itself and not at the monitor. You have the document in front of you. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, no, it's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underneath your name is the name "Nikola Bralo". Is he your brother?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that his signature below yours?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these two signatures the same?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. Someone signed. They are both signatures, but they are neither my signature nor my brother's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The time of your mobilisation is stated as the 8th of April, 1992, until the 10th of December, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I know it's not, because I didn't sign this, and somebody probably put this there because of the shares, so I would get more shares. But it's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the date here says that you were mobilised. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were employed in UNPROFOR, could you have at the same time been an active member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, I couldn't have been, because I was working in UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you tell us when you were mobilised for the first time and, in your opinion, from what time were you a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: The 19th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you employed before that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: In the British UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is why you claimed that this information in Exhibit 353 is not correct; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree. This is not mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your brother's signature?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain this, that both signatures are exactly the same?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I see that they are the same because someone signed it, but it's neither my signature nor my brother's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you knew Franjo Kovac, who is your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when he was mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: He was mobilised at the same time that I was, on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the complete date?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: The 19th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he mobilised before that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is the date there a different date in his case also?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: As far as I knew him, he would come here. But he lived in Novi Travnik and was employed there, so he wasn't mobilised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they know about him or not?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would they know about him when he spent more time with his parents than in his own house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: He would only come from time to time. He had a job.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I would now like to show you an aerial photograph, and that will be the last part of my examination. Would the usher please hand the exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D37/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo --

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please circle the house of Nikola Omazic on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you mark it with "A"?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll now read something to you. Kijazim Ramic made a statement on the 16th of February, 1995, so if the Prosecutor does not object, I would like to read only one sentence, and I would like you to put the circle around his house. Then I will ask you a question about this.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says in the statement, which was given after both conflicts so I suppose it refers to both, it says, "I saw Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic in camouflage uniforms and armed. They did not kill anyone." Would you please now circle Kijazim Ramic's house? Would you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Susak. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, as we ruled yesterday, you can't cite from a statement of a witness who has not been called. You may call this witness, but this is not evidence, so we will regard this as inadmissible and we will disregard whatever has been said. Please don't read out any statement from people who have not come to court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I accept this, but I did say "if the Prosecutor did not object." The Prosecutor did not object, but that does not matter now. I will just put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should nevertheless like to say something. [Indiscernible]... was authorised Mr. Susak to read things of this kind again, and after all, it is up to the Court, of course, to control what is being said and what is being used, but Mr. Susak should have asked for the authorisation to quote something from the statement which was given to the Prosecution. However, it seems to me that it is really questionable, and not to use another word, to show to this witness something to equate a witness who said that Mr. Josipovic did not kill anyone. At any rate, this is referring to the first conflict and not the second conflict. It's quite true that this statement was taken after the second conflict, but it is very clear, and this is something that I can testify here, this witness -- this [indiscernible] witness is referring to the 20th of October, '92, and I think it is wholly questionable when somebody just reads out that statement just like that and then try to adduce it as a kind of evidence. That is all that I had to say. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did not think it would be evidence, because you ruled on this yesterday, but this was just a kind of aid on the basis of which I would ask questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo, would you please tell me, have you marked Kijazim Ramic's house? Would you now put number "1" next to Nikola Omazic's house and number "2" next to Cazim Ahmic's (sic) house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Kijazim Ramic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ramic, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now put an arrow to indicate the direction from Kijazim Ramic's house to Nikola Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the direction of Kijazim Ramic's house, do you have a view of the road where Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic were moving on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, because it's just a few metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Kijazim Ramic have seen him that morning, considering the position of the windows on his house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The windows of Kijazim Ramic's house, do they face the house of Nikola Omazic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: They face -- some windows face the other house and some windows face the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Kijazim Ramic have seen from his window Naim Ahmic's house, Muzafer Puscul and where --

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that position, was there a view of Muzafer Puscul's house and Fahran Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, there was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a view?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. You could see the house of Fahran Ahmic and Muzafer Puscul.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark Muzafer Puscul's house with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now mark or circle the houses of (redacted) and Asim Ahmic with "B", "C", and "D"?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you done it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure of this?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment, just a moment. I don't see very well on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you find the Ogrjev warehouse, you'll orient yourself better, and if you have marked anything incorrectly, would you please cross it out. So these are the houses of (redacted), and Asim Ahmic. Would you now draw a line between (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one were to look from (redacted) house or stable toward the road and toward the houses of (redacted) and the others, would an average person have been able to observe a group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because some witnesses said they saw a group of witnesses (sic) moving toward Muzafer Puscul's house or, rather, from that to the road and toward the houses of (redacted), and Asim Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have been told that in the transcript, it says "a group of witnesses." I think it should be "a group of soldiers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would now like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go into private session. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session) Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bralo. I'm one of the counsel for the Prosecution, and I should like to ask you several questions on the basis of your testimony. I should like to know, Mr. Bralo, how were you recruited by the British battalion as a stoker? How is it that you found that job?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: My father-in-law worked as a stoker, and then they needed another worker, so my father-in-law asked me would I like to join, and I said yes. I went there and talked to a captain there, and they suggested that I come, and that is how I came and began to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that a British soldier gave you a uniform. I didn't quite understand whether it was really an army uniform, or was it working clothes, simply? What was it, precisely?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It was -- well, sort of green, olive-grey, something like that, trousers, and a camouflage jacket, whatever you call it, and that is what I used when I went to work. Since I worked in the boiler room, and that's not a particularly clean job, so I used it. It had pockets on the side and longer -- quite a deep pocket, actually, on the side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this camouflage jacket was given you by a British soldier?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. Both the trousers and the jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were the clothes that you had on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, did you also have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I took it when I went from my house towards Anto Papic's stable. I took it from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this means, if I understand you properly, that as of the moment when you left your house that morning, you were armed with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, not quite straight away, but I had to go back, because we often moved between this house and the stable and Nikola Omazic's house. When I went into the house for the second time, it was then that I picked up the rifle and started for Anto Papic's house -- stable, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain, why did you think it was necessary to arm yourself with a weapon to go to Anto Papic's stable? What was the reason behind it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, what could I do? There were women and children, somebody else might have taken it, and I had it already, so it was safer to have it with me than leave it in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a weapon was that? Can you specify it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: You mean my rifle?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: An old M48 rifle. That's what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, Mr. Bralo, that after the Kovac family arrived, you remained outside your house with your neighbour, Franjo Kovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us that at that moment, you saw Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic at some five (sic) or sixty metres away from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It is, yes. I was in front of my house and they were at the crossroad. Franjo Kovac and I started towards the stable, and they started towards Franjo Kovac's house -- that is, where he lived, and that was the house of his father-in-law, Nikola Omazic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, I want to interrupt to ask about the crossroads. The witness has produced or has marked an aerial photograph, D37/4. If that could be put in front of him, perhaps he could mark on it or show us where the crossroads to which he is referring are.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: This is my house, and that is the crossroad down to Anto Papic. Up there is Nikola Omazic and my house to the right (indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo, can you point to where the crossroads are? At the moment, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. President, that the witness has some problems with this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo, could you please show us a place which is in the direction of the Lasva River from your house; that is, down the slope? Is that where you saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic the first time that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No. No. No, here, at this crossroad, in the direction of Nikola Omazic's house (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see better in this way? If we turn the photograph, is it easier for you now to get your bearings?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, it is not. This is the road, the asphalt road towards Radak's Bridge; that is, towards the Lasva, towards the river. Here it is, the bridge (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now find the place where you were standing with Franjo Kovac at the moment when you spotted Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic? Perhaps you could start from your house. Find your house first, and then show us where that particular place is in relation to your house.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: This is my house (indicating), and we were here, on the balcony; I, Franjo Kovac. Then we started here, towards the crossroad, but we were down below it, towards Anto Papic's stable, and they started upward, towards Nikola Omazic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show us these particular crossroads in relation to your house. Where is that crossroads?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: This is the lane to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to "the crossroads," you are referring to the intersection between the road which goes down to your house and the lane which goes to Nikola Omazic's -- to Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes -- no. No, Anto Papic is to the left, and I'm like this, and there is the lane which goes down (indicating). Nikola Omazic is at the slightly higher ground, on a plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, to clarify it, we shall show the witness another photograph. Perhaps it will be easier than to identify the site.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 370.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you find your way around this map?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I can, yes. Yes, I can. Much better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then show us your house, please?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now indicate the crossroads that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is the intersection between the lane which goes down to your house and another lane which goes from Anto Papic's house to the main road?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, to Nikola Omazic's house, then Ramic's house, and then on towards the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point on this map that place where you were with Frano Kovac that morning when you noticed Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic for the first time? Where were you at that moment?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Here (indicating) in front of -- right in front of the house, about a metre from the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please put an "A" there? Will you please put the letter "A" next to that place?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now will you mark on this photograph the place where Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic were at the time when you saw them for the first time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please then put the letter "B" next to it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance between these two points, in your judgement?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Fifty or sixty metres. I did not really count them, but you have a good view because this lane goes down a little bit, but you can see. You do get a full view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no doubt in your mind. You had no problem. You had absolutely no obstacle, nothing, at this distance of 50 to 60 metres, to see Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, nothing at all. I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing at that moment?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Papic had a camouflage uniform, and Drago Josipovic had only a vest, an army vest, and civilian trousers. I don't know what kind. I really wasn't looking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I did not see anything at that moment, but an hour later I saw that he had a rifle with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did you see Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic at that crossroads, at those crossroads for the first time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Half past 5.00, perhaps a minute or two later, as they came out of the house, and I cast a look and I saw them in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment, could you look at your watch or a clock?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No. I didn't have a watch on my wrist, and we do not have a clock on the wall. We usually have some small clock somewhere in the house, but, no, I didn't look at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you mentioned the hour which you just mentioned, it is just an estimate?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, that was -- I usually got up at half past 5.00 because I had to go to work, so by the time I would be ready and had my coffee, that was about the time when I had to go to work. So that was the time when I got up, as a rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic for the first time at that place which you pointed on this map, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: What they were doing? What could they be doing? They were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but my question is were they about to start in some direction, were they moving, or were they standing?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: They were standing, but then Frano Kovac and I started from Anto Bralo's house to Anto Papic's stable. They set towards -- they set off towards Nikola Omazic's house, and we set off towards Anto Papic's stable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see them again?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: A few minutes later, perhaps ten minutes later, by the time that Anto Papic and I crossed over to the stable. (redacted) and three children and her daughter-in-law came along, and Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic were with them, reached Anto Papic's house and entered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that that day you spent in the vicinity or in the stable of Anto Papic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: In front of the stable, my house, Nikola Omazic's house, yes, that was roughly that area, because we dared not go up towards the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear and could you see in the direction of the road?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: We heard gunfire. All we heard was gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see anything?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, I couldn't, because I wasn't going up there. I mostly stayed down in my house, and this stable, there was a wall there, and that is where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, but all that day you did not see the smoke coming out from the burning houses?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from my house one could see the smoke, one could see the smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I did not see any soldiers because my house is slightly lower than Nikola Omazic's house. I could see anyone -- if there was anyone, I could see them only had I climbed up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But, Witness, you did climb up, because you did go to Anto Papic's stable. You went to Anto Papic's stable, so you had to go up the road to this intersection and then turn left, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, no. No, you are wrong, because in front of my house the ground is level, there is a very slight slope towards Anto Papic's slope, and we are going below the road towards this -- we were off that part of that lane because it was safer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, on the 16th of April, 1993, did you learn what was going on in Ahmici at any time during that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I could see, but I did not learn anything. We were talking about what could it be, because there was gunfire and things were happening up there on the higher ground, and we did not move in the direction of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, now I should like to move into private session, because I want to raise the question mentioned by a protected witness. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: 1 (redacted) 2 (redacted) 3 (redacted) 4 (redacted) (Open session)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to go back to the situation that you described to us referring to the 16th of April. We have a large number of Muslim refugees driven away from those houses and all gathered in Anto Papic's house. We were told that over 30 persons were crowded in two rooms, nine metres square each, and that you, with other persons of Croat origin, you were outside. Now, why did those persons, who were all crowded and in such difficult conditions, why did they not come out and be with you outside on that day? How does one explain this situation?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Those ladies and those gentlemen who were in Anto Papic's house could come out whenever they wanted. There was no bathroom in the house. There was no proper accommodation. It is true that there were quite a number of them. I did not count them, but they were also in the passage and in the sitting room and in the kitchen. True, there were quite a number of them. They were really crowded there. They were packed in there. So they would come out once in a while, or go to the toilet, and then return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but why were there no Muslim refugees in your house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I don't know. The door was open to anyone who wanted, who had fled from the road. So they could have come too. But presumably they went down there because they knew Anto Papic better, and he is an elderly man, and he is also -- he has been living in the village for a very long time. He was a local man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all these women mostly went to Anto Papic because they knew him, and so they were in those pretty horrible conditions that were described to us?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose, because they knew Anto best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm now moving on to the next day, to the 17th of April. Do you remember if some persons of authority came to Anto Papic's house that morning?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: As a far as I know, there were those villagers, local people. (redacted), with her mother and children; Cazim Ramic; Hasim Ahmic, with his wife and his daughter-in-law and their children, they were there. And on the 17th, I don't know, in the morning, anyway, they went towards the road with Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as you remember, when was it that they went towards the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are sorry, we couldn't understand the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Hasim Ahmic and his children? Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Fahrudin Ahmic -- not Fahrudin Ahmic, his father, Hasim, and his mother, Fahran's mother and daughter-in-law and children, they were at Anto Papic's, and Hasim Ahmic was there with his children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall rephrase my question. Do you remember if, on the 16th April, some decisions or some orders were issued regarding the removal of bodies?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember anything about that, nor did I hear anything about that from anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who and how decided that all the refugees should be taken to Zume?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, somebody, it must have been somebody in the civil defence, somebody who had the authority, because the conditions were so bad, and the man couldn't provided any food for those people. He could not feed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summary of your statement sent us by Mr. Susak, it says that somebody from the civil defence in Vitez said that women and children should be removed and be taken to Pican's coffee shop. Is that what you told Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they were taken, but not to the coffee shop, but the house was quite spacious, and they were taken there until UNPROFOR came and collected them from there. From what we knew, they were told they would be taken in the direction of Zenica. But where they were taken, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "somebody from the civil defence in Vitez"? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I don't mean anything. I didn't talk to those people, I didn't communicate with them, so I didn't know. And I was at home, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see those people?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that it was somebody from the Vitez civil defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I don't know who it was. Anto perhaps -- Papic, he speaks some German, and he communicated with him. We did not move much around, but he said that UNPROFOR would take them over, that he would be taken there to Pican's coffee shop, and Anto went with them. Because this coffee shop, it was a rather large house, it was a two-storied house, so the refugees were taken there. And when did UNPROFOR come and take them away, I don't know. I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you have a very vague memory of that period of time, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have a watch. I could not really follow -- I couldn't really know when things were happening.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to remember if you say that you forgot things. I should simply like to make a difference between what your personal recollection is and the assumption as to what happened or what you were told that had happened. As regards this civil defence in Vitez, you seem to be very vague.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I did not communicate with them at all, with those people.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly what you did that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The interpreters are insisting that you should speak into the microphone, closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: On the 17th, in the morning, Franjo Kovac and Drago Josipovic came to my house around 9.00, or half past nine, it could have been, 9.30, something like that. Drago then went home to feed the livestock, and we went to Marija Papic's, to the right from my house, across a meadow. We went there to feed her cows and pigs and hens so that they wouldn't die.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes? That is all you remember about that day, about the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: The 17th, yes. Then we returned, and we were told then, on the way, that they had gone with Anto Papic, those people who had been in his house had gone up to Pican's coffee shop, or rather to a house above Pican's coffee shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I heard that they went off in the direction of Zenica. That is what I heard, that UNPROFOR took them in the direction of Zenica, but where, exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who could tell you that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Papic went up there with them, and when he came back home, he told us -- and he was also looking for milk and some clothes, because Mirsad Osmanac had a small baby. He had two older boys of six and seven, and they were looking for some clothes and milk for that one-year-old baby. My wife gave him some clothes and poured him some milk, and by the time Anto Papic had gone back up there, UNPROFOR had already taken them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. I should merely like to tender exhibit number 370. Any objections? I should like to add, Mr. President, that I was referring to 266, not 262.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: They are admitted into evidence. Counsel Susak, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Susak:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bralo, you said that you saw Anto Papic on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you about UNPROFOR being up on the road, or was it someone else?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: He said that about UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else tell you about UNPROFOR besides Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, nobody else told me about it. Because he could speak a little German.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the Prosecutor's question, you replied that you had seen smoke from your house. Where did you see it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Across the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So over the road, across the road, to the north of the Busovaca/Vitez road?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, the Busovaca/Vitez road, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any Muslim's house near Anto Papic's house or your house was burnt down?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No, not on the 16th, but yes, on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose house burnt down on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Cazim Ramic's house. His house was burnt on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any other Muslim house burnt down?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: In the area of my lane, no other houses were burnt down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims in Anto Papic's house on the 16th of April, 1993, come to your house or Nikola Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Hasim Ahmic and his wife came to my house, because she knew my wife, so they came in -- she came in. She talked with her. I didn't go in. I stood outside with Hasim. We chatted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Muslims able to go in and out of Anto Papic's house all day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they could go in and out as they liked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the door of his house locked?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please say whether you remember which of the Croats were in your house on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: As far as I remember it was Marija Papic with her two sons; Simo Vidovic and his wife; Jozo Santic. These are all elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could any of the Muslims have come to your house and stayed there if they had wanted to?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Of course. My next-door neighbours could have come the same way that they went to Anto's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more question. On the 17th -- I apologise, on the 16th of April, 1993, did you go to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I was there in the evening. It could have been about 8 p.m. or half past 8.00. I had run out of cigarettes, so I asked Mrs. Ramic, and she gave me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's her name?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Zilka. Zilka Ramic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was with you?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Franjo Kovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Before you entered Anto Papic's house, did you come across any Muslims, either in his yard or in his house or in your house or in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: I saw Hasim Ahmic and (redacted). They were at my house, and all the others were in front of Anto's house or walking up and down the road towards the house of Nikola Omazic, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the sake of clarity, one more question. We keep referring to the crossroads above your house. Would you please tell us whether there is a road leading to Rovna, and then from Rovna to the main road, near Drago Josipovic's house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: No. There is a road behind and in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask another question: The road from Rovna which passes through Anto Papic's courtyard, does it pass by Nikola Omazic's house toward the road?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: It passes by Anto Papic's house, Nikola Omazic's house, and then it goes on toward the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is there a junction leading to your house from that road?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, it connects with that road. It's our main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is not a crossroads, because all of us are wrong, but that this is rather a road from which another road turns toward your house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Susak. I have a question. I have a question for you, Mr. Bralo, relating to the way you spent the 16th of April, '93, and the account you gave us in response to a question put to you by Counsel Susak. Now, I understand from your testimony that you were 39 years old; you were wearing a sort of military uniform, UNPROFOR, some sort of uniform; you were carrying a rifle, an M48; and you spent the whole day moving between your house, the house of Anto Papic, and the stable of Anto Papic, and in between, you fed pigs and the poultry. Now, this is on a day when something --

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: -- let's say fighting happened, a lot of fighting, firing, houses being burned, and as I say, a lot of firing, starting at about 5.20. And so you moved around with a rifle, feeding pigs and poultry. So it's -- I mean, I'm mystified. It seems so implausible. Could you give us a more detailed account of what you did on the 16th of April, '93?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, I was at home, as I said. We went to the stable of Anto Papic, came back. The second time I came home I took my rifle again, and we went to Anto Papic's stable because it was the safest there. There was a thick stone wall. Marija Papic, who came up to my house, asked me and Franjo Kovac to go -- because her house is next to the road, so she asked either me or Franjo to come, and since both of us went to Marija's house, we fed her livestock and then we came back. It was -- we had to cross some meadows and the wood to get there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But look, I mean, Ahmici is a small village. I understand it has about 500, 600 inhabitants. It's not New York or Tokyo. So you are in a small area, you hear a lot of firing, people shooting, even with heavy -- I mean, with guns and an anti-aircraft gun, and so on, and you go around, you don't ask yourself what is happening, you don't try to go to see where the people are being killed, wounded. You remain in your area, and you feed the poultry, the poultry, the pigs, and you have a chat with your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: Well, who would go up on the road when there was gunfire there? Who would have the heart to go out into the open and be shot by a bullet or hit by a shell or something like that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But then why were you carrying a weapon? If you wanted simply to hide or to get shelter, you could remain in your house the whole day without carrying a gun.

utterances.speaker: ANTO BRALO
utterances.text: There were women there, quite a lot of women, children, elderly people. So to stop them from being worried, I carried my gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Bralo. Thank you for testifying. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, yes, I should ask a question of the Prosecutor. Counsel Susak produced this document signed by Mr. Terrier, and I am not clear. Well, I think you are not tendering this in evidence, so it should be returned to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I said that I wished to tender all the documents that were discussed today into evidence. After I completed my examination in chief, I proposed that all these documents, including the one in question, should be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right, thank you. All right, it is admitted into evidence. Before we adjourn, let me make a few points. First of all, we will now reconvene on the 5th of July for three weeks. We have already received from Counsel Susak a list of witnesses, two witnesses you intend to call when we reconvene, and I hope that Counsel Pavkovic as well will hand over a list of witnesses. I should also say that on the 12th of July, we will hear a Court witness, the anthropologist we have called. She will be coming here to testify on the 12th of July, which I think is a Monday, so therefore there will be a sort of interruption in the flow of Defence witnesses. But this is the only day when she can come and stand, so we will see whether we can hear her either on the 12th or the 13th. Then I would like to clarify one point which I think is not very clear from the transcript. The ruling we made this morning about the accused testifying, I mentioned final statements by the accused, but I was referring, of course, -- I hope this was clear -- to the Nuremberg experience where these statements were made. In our case, we want to confine ourselves to hearing the accused as witnesses if they decide to testify in court at the end of the Defence case and, if need be, at the stage of rejoinder, but we don't intend to give them the opportunity to make a final statement at the end of the whole trial. We don't think it is appropriate, because they will, in any case, have an opportunity to testify twice; first of all, at the end of the Defence case, and then, if you wish to do so, at the stage of rejoinder. I wanted to make this clear because, as I say, I think it is not clear from the transcript and probably I was not clear enough this morning. Are there any matters to be discussed before we adjourn? Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, a very short question regarding the anthropologist that you mentioned and who is to testify on the 12th of July. This was a witness for the Prosecution formerly. Do you think that it will be possible for the Prosecution to see her, to meet her before her testimony, or do you think that would not be advisable? (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Since she's a Court witness, we think that it is more appropriate for you not to meet her. Also as far as the examination and re-examination is concerned, we will ask questions, the Court will ask questions. Then it will be your turn, and then, in the end, the Defence. So the normal proceedings when we are dealing with a Court witness, not with a witness called by one of the two parties. Is it clear? We will, in a way, start with a sort of examination in chief, then the Prosecutor, and then Defence counsel. Any other questions? Any matters? Defence counsel want to raise any matters? No. All right. Well, then thank you, and we'll adjourn now until the 5th of July at 9.00.
